# Code Review — 2026-08-13

| Commit | Type | Change |

**Evidence base:** full diffs of the three code-touching commits, the new test files (`configkit/configkit_race_test.go`, `configkit/configkit_errors_test.go`, `mcpserver/coverage_test.go`, `updatecheck/secureclient_test.go`, `updatecheck/updateapply/updateapply_test.go`), `go test -race` on HEAD, patch coverage measurement.

## Findings

No actionable findings. Specifically verified:

- **Security:** The updateapply cosign fix (`105e880`) now verifies the signature over the exact downloaded `checksums.txt` bytes instead of a re-serialized map — the previous approach would almost never have matched what goreleaser signed. The fix is covered by dedicated tests (wrong-signature and tampered-bytes cases in `updateapply_test.go`). No secret-bearing or auth-adjacent code was touched this cycle.
- **Concurrency:** The configkit fix (`8c2c1d3`) guards `once`/`cached`/`cachedErr` with a single `sync.RWMutex` across `Load`/`Reload`/`ResetCache`; `ResetCache` re-creates the `sync.Once` under the same lock, so there is no window where a stale `once` survives. `configkit_race_test.go` hammers all three methods from 8 goroutines × 200 iterations and passes under `-race`. The documented semantics of `Reload` (returns fresh config without populating the cache) are unchanged and intentional.
- **Tests:** The new tests are hermetic (unique app names, `t.Setenv`, no network — the secure-client tests exercise `CheckRedirect` directly with synthetic requests), use table-driven structure, and assert behavior (TLS 1.3 minimum, foreign-host redirect refusal, redirect cap) rather than implementation details. Patch coverage of the cycle's 28 changed source lines: 100%.
- **UX/DX, Architecture, Performance:** no cycle commit touches CLI surface, package structure, or hot paths. The docs commits are accurate against the code they describe (checked the PR-template and migration-notes content against `versionkit` and the v0.9.1 changes).

## Non-issues

- `configkit.Loader.Reload` not updating the cache is documented, pre-existing behavior ("bypassing the cache") — not introduced this cycle and not a defect.
- The `vectorkit/turboquant` roundtrip tests delegate assertions to the shared `testRoundtrip` helper — intentional parameterization, not zero-assert tests.

## Conclusion

The cycle shipped two well-tested bug fixes plus test/coverage improvements; nothing needs follow-up. Recommended next step: none — the only open repo-level item is the secret-scanning settings toggle from the companion audit report (`.github/audit/2026-08-13T15-03-48Z.md`).
